Low-pressure ammonia: useful rate, purge, hydrogen and full-cost contracts
ROOT, 12 November 2026 Brisbane. Conditional original engineering preparation for a future completed boundary. No current research allocation is changed, no scientist is retasked, and no physical experiment or purchase is performed. These balances are not a catalyst, ammonia plant, new measured performance or proof that every architecture fails.

The full useful operation remains 1 kg actual NH3/day from air, water and electricity, >=10 wt% aqueous product, 100 hours, <=12 kWh/kg, every component <=250 C/20 bar, with a complete $1/kg production-cost challenge at1t/day. The following is one alternative representation: an electrolyzer plus a low-temperature thermal synthesis/recovery loop. Neither the electrolyzer, nitrogen purifier, catalyst, absorber nor recycle machinery is supplied by writing that representation.

1. Stoichiometric and power interfaces
Using MNH3=17.0305g/mol and MN2=28.0134g/mol, one1kg/day module requires NET2.44659mol NH3/h,1.22330mol N2/h and3.66989mol H2/h. The useful H2 mass is0.177552kg/kgNH3. An ILLUSTRATIVE complete1bar-dry-H2 electrolyzer consuming53kWh/kgH2 therefore uses9.41026kWh/kgNH3 BEFORE loss of hydrogen, nitrogen preparation, compression, loop circulation, thermal startup, absorption and other auxiliaries. The53 figure is a hypothetical input, not a measured or quoted stack in this research. If an actual quoted electrolyzer already includes pressurization, that work cannot be added again.
Net electrolysis consumes1.58674kg water/kgNH3. A10wt% aqueous product needs another9kg solvent water/kgNH3 before water treatment, loss and startup. Those quantities are different from concentration or dilution of a tiny analytical ammonia signal.

2. An inert-recycle tradeoff derivable without a new catalyst
Consider a steady idealized thermal loop with fresh H2:N2=3:1. Fresh inert/N2 molar ratio is a, no inert is otherwise separated, all ammonia is removed between passes, and a fraction p of the remaining gas is purged. Let c be single-pass N2 conversion, F fresh N2, N reactor-inlet N2 and I reactor-inlet inert. These equations follow from actual molar conservation:
 F=[c+p(1-c)]N; aF=pI.

 u=c/[c+p(1-c)]=1-a(1-c)/s
